chapters.title: Chapter 28 - Lord Fang
paragraphs: The spiritual grass village was small, with no more than seven or eight hundred inhabitants.
It stood on the edge of a crystal-clear lake and was surrounded by a high wooden palisade.
"Who’s coming there!" roared one of the guards guarding the gates, a man at the ninth stage of Qi refinement.
"We’re disciples of the Ascending Dragon Sect, we’re here because we’ve received a mission from your Lord to deal with a giant horned wolf," replied Bao Zhang, showing his disciple token.
"Hm..." The guard examined the token for a brief moment before giving a relieved smile.

"Good of you to finally come! That damned beast has been taking everyone’s sleep away! The hunters can’t hunt anymore and even the farmers are afraid to go into their fields!" The guard opened the gate for them.
"Don’t worry, we’ll deal with this beast in no time!" Jun Hao pounded his chest with confidence, his voice hoarse and excited as Bao Zhang shook his head.
"The baron is already waiting for you at the city lord’s mansion," the guard nodded, leading the way.
"Thank you,"

Soon, they arrived at the lord’s mansion, a building far too large and luxurious for such a small village, protected by a marble wall expensive enough to probably surround the entire village with mighty stone walls.
"Corrupt son of a bitch..." Chu Yang grunted, his eyes sweeping over the luxurious garden in front of the mansion, where rare flowers and expensive ornaments glittered under the sun.
"He’s probably using the resources sent from the Sect to live in luxury instead of investing in the city! Shouldn’t we report this bastard?" Lei Feng spoke, his face contorted in disgust.
"Yes, we should, but the mission is more important," Bao Zhang shook his head.
The lord of the spiritual grass village was a former disciple who, after reaching the limit of his talent, ended up accepting the position of baron of a small village.

The ascending dragon sect’s territory was large, including hundreds of villages and many cities, so it wasn’t uncommon for disciples who no longer advanced within the sect to choose to become nobles and take over the sect’s territories.
’Some always go astray...’ Qingyi thought as he listened to the conversation.
Everyone there had been in the sect much longer than him and had lived all their lives in contact with the sect in one way or another, so he really couldn’t add much to that conversation.
"Welcome, young Taoists!" A hoarse, powerful voice drew Qingyi’s attention to the entrance of the mansion.
It was a tall, overweight man in his forties. His teeth were inlaid with gold, his fingers were covered in jewels and his robes were made of pure spiritual silk.
Being at the third stage of the foundation realm, he was certainly powerful enough to handle the beast on his own.
"Greetings, Lord Fang," Bao Zhang stopped his steps, bringing his fists together and making a respectful bow. Qingyi and the other three also did the same.
"No need for so much formality! Come on in, let’s eat and discuss this damn beast!" Lord Fang laughed, leading them through the mansion with heavy steps.

’God... how corrupt must this bastard be to live like this in such a small village?’ Qingyi thought as they entered the luxurious mansion, noticing the gold details on the walls and the rare fur rugs on the floor.

The village outside was too poor to maintain such a luxurious mansion. The houses were falling apart with thatched roofs and the palisades protecting it wouldn’t stop even the weakest mortal cultivators.
Arriving at the dining room, they were greeted by a large table covered in delicacies, liquors and wines of the highest quality.

"Come on, sit down and serve yourselves!" Lord Fang laughed, taking the center chair. Qingyi and Bao Zhang sat quietly next to him while the other three seemed to have completely lost all their contempt for the corrupt lord, focused on the food.
"Lord Fang is really very generous!" Jun Hao said, tearing off a chicken leg and stuffing it into his mouth.
Lord Fang’s smile grew as he watched everyone begin to eat, his eyes shining with satisfaction.
"Since when has the spirit beast been prowling around these parts, Lord Fang?" Bao Zhang asked, pouring himself a glass of wine.
"The first attack was about two to three months ago. Old Lin, he was one of our most respected hunters... we only found his head," Lord Fang sighed heavily, his expression momentarily gloomy.

"Since then, we’ve had attacks almost weekly. It’s being difficult to receive the Sect’s resources and people are starting to flee, so it would be good if you killed this bastard as quickly as you can."
"Don’t worry, Lord Fang, we’ll go after it today," Bao Zhang smiled, although underneath, he felt his stomach churn. He hated that kind of person, but he had to stay composed.
They finished eating quickly, sorted out a few last things with Lord Fang and left in the direction of the forest surrounding the village.
"Don’t you find that strange?" Qingyi asked as soon as they left the palisades.
"What?" Bao Zhang turned to him.
"Lord Fang, the way he received us, didn’t even try to hide anything. It’s obvious that he’s been embezzling resources from the Sect."
"It’s not strange, he’s simply sure that no one will do anything against him," Bao Zhang sighed, his eyes tired.
"We’ll kill the beast, go back to the Sect, report on what we’ve seen and the matter will probably die down there.
The Sect is too big, has too many lords and too much land.
Even the most serious cases take years to decades to conclude if they’re not a priority, and that’s if no elder puts their finger on it to delay it even further."
’It’s just like on Earth,’ Qingyi thought. No matter the organization, corruption would always exist.
It would grow more and more, and even if the leadership was honest, it would reach a level where it would simply be impossible to oversee the lower levels efficiently.
"Hurry up, we have to prepare the trap before nightfall," Bao Zhang’s order brought him out of his thoughts, and Qingyi followed right behind.

chapters.title: Chapter 29 - The giant horned wolf (1)
paragraphs: It was already afternoon when the group of disciples from the Ascending Dragon Sect arrived at the place for the trap.
Bao Zhang positioned a map he had received from one of the village hunters.
"The beast stays here during the day, it usually only comes out at night, unless it’s hungry." He pointed to a cave about a kilometer from where they were standing.
Right after that, he took a small sealed package out of his pocket.

"This is incense for attracting spirit beasts. As soon as I light it on fire, the beast will come running to us. At that point, we need to be well hidden and attack it before it sees us." Bao Zhang explained, his eyes scanning everyone present.
"Fighting it in the dark is suicide, so we should start as soon as possible. Does anyone have any doubts about my plan?"
Qingyi, who was listening carefully, just shook his head negatively, as did the other three.
"Good," Bao Zhang laughed, taking another four sealed packages out of his pocket.
"The ones I gave you before were to ward off beasts. These hide you from the beasts. It’s not perfect, but it isolates your scent enough for it to focus only on the incense of attraction."
Qingyi took the packet, feeling a faint aura of wind spirit Qi spreading through his fingers.

"I’ll attack first and hold off the beast. The rest of you, just hide behind the trees and attack as soon as I give the signal. Its skin is tough, so put all your strength into it," Bao Zhang instructed and the group split up.

Bao Zhang himself was a fist fighter, so he carried no weapons. Jun Hao used a large axe and Chu Yang wielded a sword, as did Qingyi. Lei Feng was the only one who didn’t use a melee weapon, carrying a wooden bow on his back and daggers at his waist.
Qingyi hid behind a tree, holding the thundercloud sword tightly. His eyes focused on Bao Zhang, standing in the middle of a clearing between the other four disciples.
Bao Zhang exhaled heavily, closed his eyes for a brief moment and then lit incense to call beasts before running, also hiding.
Long, torturous minutes passed as the smell of incense spread through the air. They heard nothing and felt nothing.
"Ugh... is that thing really going to come?" Jun Hao grunted, receiving looks full of disapproval.
"Shut the fuck up before I close it with an arrow!" Lei Feng pointed the bow at the impatient fat man, who finally quietened down.
Bao Zhang just sighed. Why did that idiot have to be like that? And worst of all, it was he who would have to break the news to Jun Hao’s family after the fool had killed himself.
At that moment, everyone there felt a chill. Even the courageous Jun Hao shrank into a corner.
In the distance, a howl echoed. It was clearly miles away, but it was as if it was right over their necks.
"It’s coming," Qingyi muttered, feeling pulses of Qi being sent in her direction. The beast seemed to be studying the area.
"Stay low and wait for my signal," Bao Zhang whispered, his voice low enough for only them to hear.
The next moment, heavy footsteps echoed and the trees shook. With a thud, a four-legged creature landed on the ground.
It was tall, easily over three meters, its fur as black as night and its eyes a deep blue. Two silver horns rose above its imposing head.
Its snout sniffed the air, snow-white teeth showing as it let out a soft growl and approached the incense, sniffing the ground.
Arriving in front of the incense, it took a long sniff before taking an exploratory lick.
The next moment, its eyes widened. An irritated growl escaped as it shook its head, trying to get that bitter taste out of its mouth.
"Now!" Bao Zhang roared. His feet sank into the ground as he advanced, his fists glowing golden before crashing down on the giant horned wolf’s forehead with a loud thud.
The beast staggered, its paws almost collapsing before it recovered, opening its mouth in a furious snarl.

A howl of pain escaped from the wolf as two arrows covered in Lei Feng’s wind qi hit its back. From the right, Jun Hao’s great axe crashed into its side, while Chu Yang’s sword slashed towards its legs.

Qingyi was last, attacking from the left. The thundercloud sword shone brightly as he threw himself forward with lightning steps. The tree he had been leaning on cracked, splitting in half as lightning streaked down its trunk.
Qingyi hit the wolf with a thud, his blade covered in lightning sword Qi tearing into the beast’s ribs. Of everyone there, he was the only one able to get past its protections and draw blood.
"Fall back now!" Bao Zhang’s thunderous voice woke everyone up.
Qingyi turned his body, pushing his feet against the beast’s side, using the lightning steps to move away.
The wolf shuddered and stumbled with the impact, a miserable, pained howl escaping its lips as its bloodthirsty eyes fell on Qingyi, all its murderous intent focused on him.
The next moment, a powerful aura surrounded the beast, its horns glowing as the air around it shuddered.
"It’s going to attack!" Lei Feng warned. The beast staggered towards Qingyi, but changed its steps, focusing on the sluggish Jun Hao.
With a hate-filled growl, it advanced. The fat man raised his axe, trying to protect himself, but it wasn’t enough.

The beast’s claws passed through the wood of his axe like toothpicks, tearing through his robes and the fatty flesh of his belly. His guts burst out in an explosion of blood as he collapsed to the ground.
"No!" Bao Zhang roared, grabbing the wolf’s head and preventing it from finishing Jun Hao off. His eyes focused on Qingyi as he used all his Foundation Realm power to hold the beast in place.
"Now!" He shouted, and Qingyi acted in the same instant, using lightning steps. His sword tore through the air in a powerful thrust towards the creature’s eyes.

sentences.text: It was already afternoon when the group of disciples from the Ascending Dragon Sect arrived at the place for the trap.
Bao Zhang positioned a map he had received from one of the village hunters.
"The beast stays here during the day, it usually only comes out at night, unless it’s hungry." He pointed to a cave about a kilometer from where they were standing.
Right after that, he took a small sealed package out of his pocket.
"This is incense for attracting spirit beasts.
As soon as I light it on fire, the beast will come running to us.
At that point, we need to be well hidden and attack it before it sees us." Bao Zhang explained, his eyes scanning everyone present.
"Fighting it in the dark is suicide, so we should start as soon as possible.
Does anyone have any doubts about my plan?"
Qingyi, who was listening carefully, just shook his head negatively, as did the other three.
"Good," Bao Zhang laughed, taking another four sealed packages out of his pocket.
"The ones I gave you before were to ward off beasts.
These hide you from the beasts.
It’s not perfect, but it isolates your scent enough for it to focus only on the incense of attraction."
Qingyi took the packet, feeling a faint aura of wind spirit Qi spreading through his fingers.
"I’ll attack first and hold off the beast.
The rest of you, just hide behind the trees and attack as soon as I give the signal.
Its skin is tough, so put all your strength into it," Bao Zhang instructed and the group split up.
Bao Zhang himself was a fist fighter, so he carried no weapons.
Jun Hao used a large axe and Chu Yang wielded a sword, as did Qingyi.
Lei Feng was the only one who didn’t use a melee weapon, carrying a wooden bow on his back and daggers at his waist.

His eyes focused on Bao Zhang, standing in the middle of a clearing between the other four disciples.

chapters.title: Chapter 30 - The giant horned wolf (2)
paragraphs: The sound of flesh tearing and bones breaking penetrated Long Qingyi’s ears, his sword plunging into the spirit beast’s eyes.
The creature howled, struggled and whimpered, but Bao Zhang held it firmly still as Qingyi thrust his blade deeper and deeper.
"Shit... it’s not enough!" Qingyi felt the beast use all its Qi to stop the blade from penetrating, with the two finally coming to a standstill.
Gritting his teeth, he channeled every drop of lightning Qi from his dantian towards the sword. The giant horned wolf shuddered as the thunderous Qi tore at its flesh and bones.
With a final burst of power, the creature managed to escape, throwing Bao Zhang against a tree as it tried to retreat.
Its steps were shaky and clumsy, its jaw opening and closing in vain attempts to bite the air, foam beginning to form in its mouth.

The Giant horned wolf crashed into a tree, its Qi flowing wildly before finally collapsing. It was still alive, but suffering terrible spasms, great gouts of blood flowing from between its sharp teeth.
"Your brain’s fucked, huh?" Qingyi smiled, satisfied. His lightning Qi had probably completely melted the creature’s brain.

Stepping on the beast’s neck, he aligned his sword with its heart, but stopped at the last moment. These creatures had value, and the beast would die soon. There was no point in damaging the corpse any further.
Taking a Qi recovery pill, he looked at Jun Hao, with Bao Zhang already leaning over him.
"Ugh... Tell my mom I died a hero." Jun Hao grunted, coughing up large quantities of blood.
"Tell her yourself, you fat bastard!" Bao Zhang snarled, shoving a healing pill down his throat as he grabbed his exposed guts and shoved them back in.
Stopping next to Jun Hao, Qingyi focused his lightning Qi on his index finger.
Bao Zhang held the two sides of the horrible wound, pressing them together while Qingyi used his lightning Qi to weld the skin and flesh together.
"Argh... fuck!" Jun Hao grunted in pain, but Lei Feng held him firmly, covering his mouth and preventing him from moving too much.
"Circulate your Qi, you idiot. Is the great Jun Hao going to die because of a little wound like that?" Lei Feng teased, his slightly trembling voice betraying his concern.
Hearing that, Jun Hao gritted his teeth and closed his eyes, concentrating on circulating his vital Qi.
"Thank you," Bao Zhang thanked Qingyi, who wiped a drop of sweat from his face as he finished closing the wounds.
Bao Zhang had completely changed his view of the handsome young man.
At first, he thought he was just a pretty face who had been lucky enough to receive a golden token in a selection where the Sect had found few talents.
But now, he had to recognize Qingyi’s true potential.

He himself was a cultivator with an eighth-level spiritual root who had just entered the foundation realm, but he wasn’t sure if he would be able to defeat Qingyi if he met him in the selection for inner disciples.
"His situation is stabilized, but he needs a doctor, and fast," Chu Yang muttered after measuring Jun Hao’s pulse.

"Junior Brother Qingyi, you’re the only one here with a movement technique. Do you think you can get Jun Hao to the village? We’ll follow right behind," Bao Zhang asked, his face contorted with worry.
Qingyi closed his eyes for a moment, feeling his Qi reserves.
’About 30%... the city must be more than five kilometers away... I’ll have to push it a bit,’ he thought, taking out another Qi recovery pill and swallowing it as he stood up.
Turning his back to Jun Hao, he said, "Put him on my back. I’ll try to get there as quickly as I can."
"Thanks again," Bao Zhang and Lei Feng picked up the fat man together, placing him on Qingyi’s back. Chu Yang took a small rope out of his pocket, tying them together.
Feeling that they were tightly bound, Qingyi stepped forward, activating the Lightning Steps. His body and Jun Hao’s disappeared in a thunderous aura that cut through the air.
Running at extreme speed through the dense forest carrying someone as heavy as Jun Hao was exhausting.
Qingyi gave it his all, already feeling his meridians begin to burn like live embers. He gritted his teeth and pushed himself beyond his limits.
When he finally reached the village gates, he felt as if his meridians were on the verge of collapse, throbbing painfully.
"I need the village doctor!" He roared at the guard.
"I’m sorry, but-" The guard shuddered, taking a step back.
"NOW!" Qingyi stomped hard on the ground, the earth beneath his feet cracking as a thread of murderous intent leaked from his piercing eyes.
He had no special friendship with Jun Hao - in fact, he even found him a bit annoying - but he couldn’t deny that the fat man had a good heart.
Qingyi didn’t want him to die at his hands.
With trembling steps, the guard turned around, running towards the residence of the only doctor in the whole village.

Arriving in front of the humble-looking clinic, Qingyi passed through the door, ignoring the angry shouts of an irritated old man who appeared to be the doctor. He entered one of the rooms and placed Jun Hao on a bed.
"Hey, what the fuck do you think you’re doing? Didn’t you see we’re closed? I’m not going to treat that bastard," the old man grunted, but his words lost their force as soon as his eyes met Qingyi’s.

"We’re disciples of the Ascending Dragon Sect and we just killed that damn wolf. You’re going to treat him, or you’re going to be the one who needs treatment." Qingyi growled. He wasn’t the kind of person who liked to use the Sect’s name like that, but the situation demanded it.
With a frightened look on his face, the old man finally lowered his head, running over to Jun Hao’s body and injecting a thread of Qi into his meridians to check his condition.
Exhausted, Qingyi just sat down outside the clinic.
After a few minutes, the figures of Bao Zhang, Lei Feng and Chu Yang finally appeared on the horizon, carrying the corpse of the beast on their shoulders.

chapters.title: Chapter 31 - Lord Fang is a good-hearted man
paragraphs: Bao Zhang let the carcass of the giant horned wolf fall with a thud, entering the clinic with Chu Yang and Lei Feng close behind.
"How is he?" he asked the old doctor, approaching Jun Hao, who seemed to be sleeping peacefully.
"Hm..." The old man scratched his gray beard before smiling. "He’ll live, he just needs a good week’s rest."
Hearing the doctor’s words, everyone breathed a sigh of relief.

"Well... now why don’t we discuss payment? Your friend was quite unpleasant with me. I was closed, he forced me out of my resting hours." The old man smiled, putting his hands together as he looked at the beast outside.
Such powerful young Taoists must have had a lot of money.
"Oh, of course." Bao Zhang took out ten silver coins, placing them on the old man’s hand.
"Ten silver coins?" The old man stared at the money.
It was a good amount, a more than fair payment, but he still couldn’t stop himself from gritting his teeth. How could those young Taoists be so stingy? He wouldn’t accept less than a gold coin!

"What do you think I am, a slave? Ten pieces of silver isn’t enough for me to keep that pig alive for the face of-" The old man’s voice was interrupted when Bao Zhang’s hand fell on his shoulder, forcing him to kneel.
"You live in a Sect village, under a Sect sky, and eat Sect grain." He spoke, increasing his murderous intent with every word.
"If my junior had to force you out of your resting hours, it means that you refused to treat a disciple of the Ascending Dragon Sect. I should rip your head off for that, you know?"
Bao Zhang growled, glaring at Chu Yang.
"Your sword, now." He ordered, and Chu Yang obeyed without question.
"N-no!" The old man fell to his knees, tears forming in his eyes. Weren’t those pure and gentle disciples? Why would they kill him just for wanting to extort them honestly?
"I-I made a mistake, please forgive me, it won’t happen again, never again!" The old man begged, prostrating himself and crawling over to Bao Zhang, kissing his shoes.
"Ugh..." Bao Zhang grunted queasily, stepping back and handing Chu Yang his sword.

"We’ll be back early in the morning. Spend the night looking after our friend. If he dies, I’ll consider it your negligence." Bao Zhang’s voice echoed in the old man’s ear as he walked towards the door.
That old man was a fox and understood the threat well.
Long Qingyi, sitting outside the clinic, couldn’t hold back his laughter.
He had heard everything clearly and was glad that Bao Zhang treated old bastards with the same "affection" as he did.
"You’re a mess," Qingyi smiled at his three companions.
"Really? And why don’t you look at yourself?" Lei Feng held back a giggle as he watched Qingyi.

Everyone was dirty with blood and sweat at some point, but Qingyi was totally drenched. His white robes were red and even the pale skin of his face looked as if it had received a large coat of scarlet paint.
"Well, I worked the hardest," Qingyi laughed, standing up with a grunt and looking at the wolf.

People were already beginning to gather around the colossal corpse. Some of the braver ones even touched the fur of the beast that had tormented them for so long, their eyes filled with gratitude as they stared at the young heroes.
"I think we need a good bath," the handsome, blood-soaked young man said.
"Hm... there must be at least one inn in this town," Chu Yang commented.

"Inn? Lord Fang is a good-hearted man. I’m sure he’ll offer us a hot bath and a noble bed as soon as we present our hunt to him." Qingyi stretched as she grabbed the wolf’s body. Circulating his Qi, he grunted as he lifted it.
"Junior brother Qingyi really is a very intelligent man," Lei Feng let out an excited sigh as he followed him.
Even Bao Zhang, the most composed and mature among them, couldn’t help but laugh slightly.
It wasn’t long before they arrived at the Lord’s mansion and were greeted by a smiling Lord Fang.
"Back already? I thought it would take you days to hunt this bastard down! The Sect’s younger generation really has improved a lot compared to when I was a disciple."
Lord Fang slapped Qingyi hard on the shoulder, crouching over the wolf’s carcass without caring about the blood staining his hands when he came into contact with the young man.
It really was an impressive beast. He had seen few so powerful for his level of cultivation in his entire life.
"Twenty gold coins, what do you think? Five coins each." Lord Fang stood up. The carcass was worth a little more, but that was his share for taking care of the processing.
"Twenty-five," Bao Zhang said. "Our other companion is still alive, he’s just being treated."
"Oh... I’m sorry. Then twenty-five is a good price."
Lord Fang took some coins out of his pocket and handed them to the group leader, who smilingly handed them out.
They were a little richer, both with the thousand Sect contribution points and a few extra gold coins.
"Come on in. I’ll ask the servants to prepare a bath and a comfortable bed for you. I can’t allow such talented young people to sleep in miserable taverns."
Qingyi couldn’t help exchanging glances with the others. This was exactly what he had said would happen!
As they approached the mansion’s large double doors, he noticed a woman in elegant clothes watching them with a casual smile.
The woman wore no make-up, and none was needed, her skin, pale as snow and as perfect as the finest jade had a natural blush, and her lips were full and rosy.
She had long black hair that fell on her delicate shoulders and penetrating green eyes, her voluptuous body covered by a luxurious tight green dress.
From a thin waist, her hips extended smoothly, and above it, large voluptous breasts.
Observing such beauty, Qingyi shuddered slightly.
She was the most beautiful women he had ever seen. Hua Feiyan and Mo Feixue were nowhere near her.
What was a woman of that caliber doing there, with an weak, corrupt Lord like Fang? It didn’t make sense!

This meant that she was from the nine peaks basin, and not only that - she was one of the most powerful cultivators in that region.

"Oh... that’s my daughter! Fang Meili," smiled Lord Fang, patting the woman on the shoulder.
’Daughter? What the hell is this bastard talking about? This woman must be at least three times his age!’ Qingyi thought, but his eyes soon fell on his companions.
They had calm gazes, in fact, even a little nauseous, as if looking at that girl’s face was torture. Those were not the eyes of someone who had just seen such a heavenly beauty.

’Calm down... there must be an explanation for this, perhaps an artifact of illusion? She’s a poison master, so that could be it... but how can I see her real form?’ Qingyi closed his eyes for a moment, but when he opened them again, he saw her eyes focused on him.

"It’s a pleasure to meet such talented young cultivators, I hope you’ll look after me when I get to the Sect." She smiled as she bowed to them, the voice Qingyi heard was not that of a beautiful, delicate woman.

’No chance, this has to be some kind of illusion artifact... my draconic eyes should be able to see through it.’

After a few moments, servants appeared, taking the group to their rooms.
Taking off his bloody clothes and throwing them into a corner, Qingyi looked around. It was a large, luxurious room, with a bed spacious enough to fit five people.
Shaking his head, he entered the bathroom, where a tub of steaming water was already waiting for him.
He sat down with a tired grunt, feeling the hot water wash the blood from his body. The sensation was pleasant, the warmth relaxing his tense muscles after the long journey.

"Miss Ta- I mean, Miss Meili? I don’t think you being here is appropriate..." He hastily corrected himself, looking away.
"What do you mean? Dad only asked me to see if everything was all right."
She smiled gently, her eyes taking on a slightly more serious expression as she asked.
"So Young Master Qingyi, I quite like your eyes..." She crouched beside his bathtub, her eyes studying Qingyi’s face.

Nghn~..." another muffled moan escaped Tang Biyue’s lips, the sound resounding off the bathroom walls.
’I’m so fucking dead!’ Qingyi’s face finally showed a hint of despair.

He had thought that even after improving his bloodline, he wouldn’t need to go to Feixue’s wedding to reach the foundation realm and prepare for the disciple selection.
But now he wasn’t sure.
He still had a few months to prepare, but if he couldn’t meet Feiyan, Feixue would probably be his only option.
Even so, Qingyi didn’t complain too much about the price increase.
He now had some idea of how this system worked - it was like the MMORPG games on Earth.

He had no doubt that when he reached the level of a woman like Tang Biyue, the price for a single level of cultivation would be hundreds of thousands, maybe even millions.
Letting out a long sigh, he stood up, looking outside. It was already late and that was the day of Feixue’s wedding, which was due to start in a few hours.

He didn’t have much interest in such things and, honestly, he wasn’t sure if he’d get any kind of lust point out of it, since the wife would be with her husband the whole time.
There wasn’t much room for him there, was there?

’Fuck it... in the worst case, I’ll drink and eat for free.’ He stood up, cracking his neck before taking a good shower and putting on his usual pure white robe.
After making sure he looked presentable, he set off from the Sect towards the Yang family residence.
The mansion was buzzing with activity.
The commoners gathered outside, trying to catch a glimpse of the ceremony, while luxurious carriages arrived through the wide central gate.
Sect elders, select disciples, other powerful families from the region and even representatives from trade guilds were present.
Qingyi felt a little overwhelmed by the atmosphere, but he just lowered his head and approached the gate.
"Hold it right there!" The guard growled in his direction. "Only guests may enter, the commoners must watch from outside."
Qingyi didn’t even bother to reply, simply showing his invitation envelope.
After a brief glance at the emblem and confirmation of its legitimacy, the guard stepped aside, allowing him to enter.
Qingyi entered the mansion and walked through the large central garden, surrounded by pompous and arrogant nobles.
A few young women caught his eye, smiling at him whenever their gazes met, but none of them were noteworthy - mediocre talents and appearances, with insignificant rewards.
"Young Taoist Qingyi! You’ve come!" An excited voice called out to him.
When he turned around, he saw Tianran smiling and, next to him, a middle-aged man whose robes bore the symbols of the Mo family.
"Uncle Wuchen, this is Long Qingyi, that young Taoist who helped us on the road!" Tianran introduced him to the man next to him.
"This humble one pays respects to senior," Qingyi bowed to Wuchen.
Qingyi couldn’t feel Wuchen’s power, but he could tell that he was at least at the Iron Body realm.
"No need for such formalities, young man. It’s good to see such talented juniors in the Sect of the Ascending Dragon.
I still remember when I was a disciple there. It’s been two hundred years, but things have changed a lot, hahaha!"
Wuchen laughed, his voice soft and friendly as he patted Qingyi firmly on the shoulder.
He seemed like a pleasant man.

"Come on, we’ve just been waiting for you. The ceremony should begin shortly," said Tianran, guiding Qingyi and Wuchen into the mansion’s grand central hall, large enough to accommodate thousands of people.
Qingyi sat down next to Tianran and Wuchen.
The three of them chatted about life in the Sect while enjoying the Yang family’s vast collection of wines and spiritual liquors.
It wasn’t long before the main moment of the occasion arrived, and everyone fell silent.

"It’s a pleasure to have you all here at my residence. Today, I am very happy to announce the union between the Yang and Mo families.
May the heavens bless this marriage and may this alliance last for the next thousand years."
The moment his voice fell silent, everyone celebrated. In the distance, the bride and groom finally appeared.
Young Master Yang was wearing a blue robe, his long black hair perfectly tied up while his face showed a peaceful smile.
Mo Feixue, on the other hand, wore a pristine white dress, her back covered by a robe that was slowly tinged with gold.
The ceremony was short. They exchanged vows, pledged eternal loyalty before the heavens, and the feast began, with food and drink being served at will.
Qingyi remained in a corner, drinking and chatting casually with Tianran.
From time to time, he exchanged provocative glances with Feixue, but it didn’t go any further than that.
Everyone left by the time the couple finally went up to their room. Young Master Yang was so drunk that he could barely walk and had to be carried by the bride.
Qingyi had also drunk a lot, but barely felt the effect - his bloodline and constitution made him practically immune to it.
As he walked past the Yang family gardens, he noticed the window of the couple’s bedroom open.
’I hope that bastard passed out from drinking so much.’ A mischievous smile appeared on his lips as he activated the Lightning Steps.

The young archer was already at the ninth stage of the Qi Refining Realm when they killed the giant horned wolf a few months ago, but he hadn’t expected the boy to advance in such a short space of time.
He continued to scan the names, his eyes landing on a name in the top right corner.
Xu Tianming.
He had promised that he would kill Long Qingyi in the internal selection of disciples, and that day had finally come.
With his current power, Qingyi didn’t fear anyone in that selection, but he couldn’t help feeling a twinge in his heart when he saw Feiyan’s anxious eyes.
She obviously had no feelings for Tianming and couldn’t care less about him, but remembering the promise he had made to kill Qingyi made her visibly distressed.
"Don’t worry, your husband still has a few tricks up his sleeve." Qingyi laughed lightly, holding her waist a little more firmly.
"uhm-mm," Feiyan snuggled into his arms.
Her closeness drew the attention of many male disciples, but she didn’t mind.
Unfortunately, a loud voice soon broke their moment.
"Junior Brother Qingyi, it’s good to see you here!" Bao Zhang smiled as he approached the couple.
Qingyi turned around, returning the smile.
Behind Bao Zhang, he saw Lei Feng and Jun Hao, their eyes shining as they noticed Feiyan’s presence.
The fat man was the first to gather his courage and step forward.
"So, big sister Feiyan... what’s your relationship with-"
"Respect." Bao Zhang’s loud voice interrupted him, along with his fist to the fat man’s head, who stumbled, almost falling over.
Without giving him a chance, Bao Zhang forced him to prostrate himself, also lowering his own head.
"I beg your pardon for my friend’s loose tongue, Senior Sister Feiyan.
He was born prematurely and his brain turned out to be underdeveloped." Bao Zhang apologized.
Even though Hua Feiyan was with a friend of theirs, for outer disciples like them, offending inner disciples usually meant death, while offending core disciples often resulted in much worse.
The Ascending Dragon Sect was fair, but it wasn’t kind, and power was often necessary to have justice.
"Don’t worry about it." A restrained giggle escaped Feiyan’s beautiful red-painted lips, her eyes sweeping over the three men.
"And yes, I’m Qingyi’s wife.
It’s a pleasure to meet the husband’s friends."
Hearing those words, Lei Feng and Jun Hao turned completely red.
They had already imagined that this was the case, but hearing it from her own mouth made everything completely different.
They couldn’t help but look at Qingyi with a renewed vision.
Was it even right for them to call Qingyi junior brother?
Why not start calling him master?
They desperately wanted to know the secret to succeeding with incomparable beauties!
Fortunately for Bao Zhang’s heart, the idiots had little time to open their mouths and ask more questions, as Elder Tian’s voice caught everyone’s attention.

chapters.title: Chapter 40 - The inner disciples selection (02)
paragraphs: "Attention!" Elder Tian stopped on a large platform above the arena.
To his left, a female elder who appeared to be in her fifties; to his right, a male elder with a powerful and imposing body.
His aged eyes swept over everyone there, pausing briefly on Qingyi before an approving smile played on his lips.
He didn’t like the way that woman clung to the young man, but Feiyan had proved herself worthy, awakening an alchemy spirit root and becoming one of the sect’s most important disciples.
Shaking his head, he continued with his duty.
"There are many outer disciples challenging the selection for the inner disciples, but I must warn you that only ten will pass. The tests will be done in one-on-one combats.
These fights will end when one of the disciples dies or when one of the elders intervenes because he thinks that one of the disciples is incapable of continuing to fight.
The moment an elder intervenes, the fight must stop immediately. Killing a brother disciple in this case will lead to severe punishment."
"Does everyone understand?" The elder asked, and the whole arena responded in unison.
"Good." He laughed, looking at the scoreboard that bore the names of the two hundred disciples who would try to become inner disciples.
"Long Qingyi and Lei Feng, one step ahead!" He roared.
"I’m sorry, Brother Feng, but I think you’ll only have a chance to become an inner disciple next year," Qingyi laughed lightly.
"Don’t think so much of yourself. You’re still my junior, and I’ve come up with a new technique that will make even you tremble," Lei Feng laughed back.
"I’m excited to see it."
The two of them jumped into the arena, standing on opposite sides.
Qingyi drew the Thunderclouds sword, electric lightning dancing across the blade as a powerful aura spread through his body.
Lei Feng gripped his bow tightly, but didn’t place any arrows.
In reality, he just pulled on the empty string and, in the next moment, a stream of Qi surged from his fingers, forming a bluish arrow between them.
Qingyi couldn’t help but be surprised by this. Was it some kind of combat technique? He had never seen anything like it.
"Begin!" Elder Tian’s voice snapped him out of his stupor.
Lei Feng pulled the bowstring tight, a new layer of light dancing across the arrow before he released it towards Qingyi.
The Qi projectile tore through the air, splitting into three separate projectiles that flew at strange angles.
"That’s dangerous!" Qingyi gritted his teeth, turning his body. One of the arrows passed through his face, drawing a single, painful trickle of blood.
The second arrow hit the ground behind him with a thud, while the third collided with his sword.
A metallic clang echoed. Qingyi’s feet dragged on the ground as he contained the powerful Qi of the arrow.
When he finally won the clash and the Qi arrow disappeared, Lei Feng already had another one ready.
’It’s going to be problematic,’ Qingyi sighed before stopping for a brief moment, circulating his draconic Qi and sending it towards his eyes.
They had improved to the intermediate level when he made another breakthrough in his bloodline, but he hadn’t fully tested them yet.
Lei Feng released his arrows and the world seemed to slow down for Qingyi as he advanced towards his opponent.
His blade, covered in the Qi of the Lightning Sword, tore through the air with a piercing whistle.
He didn’t face those arrows directly, cutting towards one of the arrows, pushing it aside and causing it to hit the ground behind him.
His sword moved in a split second, perfectly deflecting the second and third arrows as he got closer and closer to Lei Feng.
"Damn it," Lei Feng took a step back, pushing all his Qi into his arms.
That was an expensive technique, but Qingyi was dealing with it without even using his movement technique. How was it possible?
He had to finish that battle as quickly as possible if he was to stand a chance.
Gritting his teeth, his eyes flashed, meeting Qingyi’s eyes as he pulled the bowstring.
The bow trembled in his hands, the wood crackling and the string so tense that it felt like it could break at any second.
Every moment he maintained this tension, a new wave of energy entered the Qi arrow, transforming its blue from a light translucent to a deep, almost palpable hue.
Qingyi stopped his steps, sensing the danger. If it hit him in the wrong place, he would be dead, he knew that.
He focused even more draconic Qi into his eyes, he could already feel his meridians burning, but he ignored the sensation.
The world seemed to slow down even more as Lei Feng released the bowstring.
A bang echoed as the arrow broke through the sound barrier, splitting into more than a dozen pieces, each flying towards Qingyi at a different angle.
"So that was your card up your sleeve?" Qingyi smiled. If it had been anyone else, they would probably have been doomed, but he was not intimidated.
His body glowed as he activated the Lightning Steps.
The moment before the arrows hit him, he leapt forward, towering over Lei Feng.
Lei Feng’s arrows hit nothing but empty air, some flying towards the audience and eliciting startled cries, only to be stopped by the arena’s protective array.
"Ugh..." Lei Feng grunted as he abandoned his bow, parrying Qingyi’s blade with double daggers.
A metallic clang echoed as he tried unsuccessfully to stop his opponent’s sword.
"Damn, you win!" He surrendered, feeling the heat of the Lightning Sword Qi coming close to his face.
"You fought well," Qingyi said with a smile, helping him to his feet before he jumped back towards his Feiyan.
The tanned beauty immediately surrounded him with care, putting a recovery pill she had made herself into his mouth.
"Mmm, thanks," he murmured, feeling the warmth of the pill spread through his body.
"Lucky bastard," Lei Feng said between his teeth as he walked away, but he couldn’t help shuddering when Bao Zhang’s deadly gaze fell on him.
"First fight, Qingyi advances!" Lord Tian’s voice caught everyone’s attention again.

chapters.title: Chapter 41 - The inner disciples selection (03)
paragraphs: "That was a good battle." Bao Zhang patted Lei Feng on the shoulder.
The young man was discouraged, he was sure he would be able to rise as an inner disciple.
Sadly, fate had been cruel in pitting him against Qingyi.
"Easy for you to say, you’re on the opposite side to that monster! By the time you meet him, you’ll already be in the finals." Lei Feng grunted, and Qingyi couldn’t help laughing.
It really was a good battle. If he hadn’t had the lightning steps, Lei Feng would certainly have won.
Qingyi was simply the worst opponent he could face.

"Look on the bright side, at least we’ll be able to become inner disciples together in the next selection!" Jun Hao joined in the conversation, but only managed to draw another despondent sigh from Lei Feng.
They didn’t even know when the next selection of inner disciples would be. It could be next year, or just in ten years.
"Yu Hanzi and Bao Zhang! One step ahead!" Elder Tian’s voice caught the attention of everyone there.
Bao Zhang jumped towards the arena, his eyes focusing on the figure in front of him.
Yu Hanzi was a tall, handsome man. Despite being a commoner, he still carried all the arrogance of a nobleman.
Like Bao Zhang, he was also a palm cultivator with an eighth-level spiritual root, and one Zhang knew well.
They had already had a few disputes over cultivate resources, and many duels to try to prove themselves the most powerful palm cultivator among the outer disciples.
One of these disputes even nearly ended in a battle to the death. Something horrible would have happened if it hadn’t been for an elder intervening.
"Don’t expect any elders to save your life this time, Bao Zhang!" Yu Hanzi growled, his fists glowing.
"Just don’t cry like a little girl when I screw up your face. I can see that your nose hasn’t fully recovered yet." Bao Zhang smiled provocatively.
"Don’t you dare!" Yu Hanzi’s face fell apart, his arrogant look turning to pure anger.
This was the greatest shame of his life.
Who did Bao Zhang think he was to talk about this publicly?
"Begin!" Elder Tian’s voice echoed through the arena and they both stepped forward.
Their hands met with powerful thuds. The marble floor cracked beneath their feet, their foundation realm cultivations exploding into golden auras.
They stood in a stalemate for a long moment before stepping back, staring at each other.
"You’re weaker than before... have you been running away from training to hook up with prostitutes again?" Bao Zhang teased, but he couldn’t help feeling his hands shaking.
Yu Hanzi had also advanced to the second stage of the foundation, and his base was no weaker than Bao Zhang’s.
This fight would be much more difficult than he had expected. Luckily, he also knew how to deal with men like Yu Hanzi.
He just needed to aim for the face.
With a confident smile, he advanced again. His fists shone as if they were covered in a veil of gold, launched straight at Yu Hanzi’s handsome face.
"No!" Yu Hanzi sensed the danger immediately and turned his body. Bao Zhang’s right palm passed inches from his face, but his left had another target.
"Argh!" A grunt of pain echoed, followed by a thud as Bao Zhang’s fist met Yu Hanzi’s chest.
The handsome young man retreated desperately, coughing up a large gulp of blood and barely able to breathe. But he didn’t surrender.
"Let’s end this!" Bao Zhang roared, appearing over Yu Hanzi and letting his fist fall on him.
"That won’t work twice!" Yu Hanzi revealed a bloody smile as he parried Bao Zhang’s fists, but regretted it the next moment.
Bao Zhang wasn’t trying to punch him.
Bao Zhang was trying to grab him!
Without even giving the handsome young man time to react, Bao Zhang grabbed his fists firmly before launching a kick towards his knees.
Yu Hanzi’s legs buckled, and he fell onto the ground.
He barely had time to cast a pleading glance towards the elders before Bao Zhang’s boots collided with his face.
With the first blow, his nose broke, his head hitting the concrete with a thud.
In the second, he lost his front teeth.
In the third, his jaw broke.
It was only on the fourth blow that one of the elders next to Elder Tian acted, his Iron Body Realm cultivation falling on Bao Zhang.
"Enough!" He landed beside him, looking at Yu Hanzi’s disfigured face, sunk in a pool of blood.
It would be difficult for him to heal from that, even with the best healing pills in the sect.
"I didn’t expect you to be so cruel," Qingyi commented as Bao Zhang returned to the stands.
"I wouldn’t be that cruel, he was begging for it," Bao Zhang laughed, drawing a surprised look from Qingyi.
It was one of the first times he had seen that man break his seriousness.
Unfortunately, his moment of relaxation didn’t last long and soon Qingyi’s face turned serious.
It was Tianming’s turn for battle.
He was on the same side as Bao Zhang and, if they both didn’t lose any battles, they would face each other in the semi-finals.
"Anyone you know?" Bao Zhang asked.
"Just an annoying fly," Qingyi replied, his eyes sweeping over Feiyan.
The bronzed beauty was calm in his arms, barely sparing a second glance as Xu Tianming descended into the arena.
Tianming was dressed differently from what he normally wore.
His robes bearing the Xu family symbol were nowhere to be seen, replaced by plain black clothes.
His cold gaze swept over everyone there, landing on Qingyi and Feiyan for a brief moment before looking forward again.
She looked much more beautiful than before, But he didn’t let himself get carried away.
He sighed heavily and drew his sword, the silver sword Qi taking on a sickly green color as it spread across the blade.
The moment Elder Tian’s voice rang out, announcing the start of the match, he threw himself forward.
His sword clashed only once with his opponent’s before he retreated.
He didn’t need more than that.
To the surprise of everyone there, the young man who had fought Tianming barely managed to take two steps forward.
There were no visible injuries, but his face took on a purple hue and he fell to his knees, unable to breathe.

chapters.title: Chapter 42 - The inner disciples selection (04)
paragraphs: Silence overtook the outer disciples’ arena as the female elder knelt beside the poisoned disciple, picked him up in her arms and carried him towards the sect’s medicine pavilion.
Elder Tian looked at Tianming with disapproval, but did nothing.
The sect was quite liberal, any kind of cultivation that didn’t directly follow the unorthodox paths was allowed.
Poison was right on the border between orthodox and unorthodox, but it hardly chose sides.
After all, medicine was just a poison in a dosage low enough not to kill. How could they ban it?
What really intrigued the elder was the origin of that power.
Tianming had a sword spirit root, had he awakened a new spirit root like Feiyan?
No, that was impossible, two miracles couldn’t happen like that in such a short period of time.
’He must have consumed some kind of poisonous essence...’ Elder Tian concluded as he shook his head.
Tianming noticed the elder’s stare, but just ignored it, his remaining eye focusing on Qingyi.
His gaze was cold and murderous. He had seen Qingyi fight and knew well that if that was all his power, it wouldn’t take more than a single blow to eliminate him.
’I can’t wait to see that bitch’s face as that damned pretty face melts under my poison!’ He exclaimed mentally as he glanced at Feiyan, imagining her begging for him.
Qingyi remained cold as his eyes met those of Tianming.
He could already imagine what was going through the young man’s mind and couldn’t help but laugh internally.
’Poison, huh? You picked one of the worst things you could use to fight me,’ Qingyi thought.

His body of the primordial dragon basically made him immune to any kind of toxic substance, and even if he was affected, it wouldn’t take long for the strands of draconic Qi in his Dantian to purify the problem.
But there was still one thing that worried him: Tianming’s cultivation.
He simply couldn’t sense it, it was as if Tianming’s cultivation was far superior to his own, to a level that Qingyi had difficulty even sensing his aura.
’That’s going to be dangerous...’
"He seems to have quite a lot of hatred for you." Bao Zhang asked, noticing Qingyi’s gaze.
"Yes, I stole Feiyan from him." Qingyi laughed lightly, feeling the bronzed beauty tremble in his arms as Bao Zhang’s eyes widened.
Long, awkward moments passed without a word being spoken.
"That’s not a joke, is it?" Bao Zhang asked, his eyes alternating between Feiyan and Qingyi without stopping.
Qingyi was a beautiful man.
In fact, if the sect had a ranking of the most attractive men, he would appear in first place; if he claimed to be second, no one would dare declare themselves first.
But even so, he was far from having the status of a young master of the Xu family.
The Xu family itself was a duke-level family of the Golden Sun Kingdom, an entity that was only a single step behind the Ascending Dragon Sect.
If their patriarch reached the Burning Blood Realm, he probably wouldn’t fall behind the three great sects of the outer region of the Blue Moon Continent.
How on earth could Feiyan choose someone like Qingyi over young master Xu?
Qingyi ignored Bao Zhang’s question and they just focused on the battles that followed, making the man sigh heavily and also mind his own business.
Lei Feng and Jun Hao, however, didn’t miss that conversation; their gazes towards Qingyi getting even brighter.
Their junior brother really was a great man! They would never have imagined stealing the wife of a young man as rich and powerful as Xu Tianming!
"Are you worried?" Qingyi whispered in Feiyan’s ear.
The beauty hadn’t said a word since the moment she saw Tianming, her eyes filtering him with coldness.
Feiyan listened to Qingyi’s words, her eyes remaining distant for a moment until she plucked up the courage to speak.
"I want you to surrender to him before the battle begins..." She finally spoke, turning her face towards Qingyi’s.
"Don’t you have confidence in your husband?" Qingyi kept a gentle smile on his face, but still felt a twinge of pain in his heart after seeing the distress on her face.
The only time he had seen her like this was when he took her as his wife.
Since then, she had always remained the smiling, seductive Feiyan who wasn’t shaken by anything.
"His cultivation... is already at the fourth stage, and has a powerful base. Even I can barely sense it... please... you don’t have to fight it," she finally said, her eyes watering.
Qingyi paused for a moment, closed his eyes, felt his heart burn, but didn’t lower his head.
"You have too little confidence in me, dear... He would have to be at least at the seventh stage of the Foundation Realm to frighten me." Qingyi spoke, hugging her comfortingly.
Her face sank into his chest, staining his white robes as he lovingly stroked her hair.
Despite his confidence, Qingyi’s eyes were cold.
Fourth stage Foundation Realm... how the hell had that bastard advanced so far in such a short space of time?
Qingyi thought about it, remembering the strange poisonous aura that surrounded his Tianming’s sword.
’System, can that be a threat to me?’ he asked.
[No, the body of the primordial dragon has total resistance to all kinds of poison and toxic substances.
Only a handful of poisons can affect it, but it’s unlikely to see any of them outside of Heavenly Heaven].
’I see...’ Qingyi looked at the horizon.
He didn’t have long to think, soon it was his turn to fight again.
"Long Qingyi and Chen Xiaohu, step forward," Elder Tian spoke, and the two young men climbed into the arena.
Chen Xiaohu was a very famous flame cultivator in the sect.
With an eighth-level flame spirit root, he was one of the favorites to become an inner disciple.
Being at the third stage of the Foundation Realm, he was a good target for Qingyi to test his new power on.

sentences.text: Silence overtook the outer disciples’ arena as the female elder knelt beside the poisoned disciple, picked him up in her arms and carried him towards the sect’s medicine pavilion.
Elder Tian looked at Tianming with disapproval, but did nothing.
The sect was quite liberal, any kind of cultivation that didn’t directly follow the unorthodox paths was allowed.
Poison was right on the border between orthodox and unorthodox, but it hardly chose sides.
After all, medicine was just a poison in a dosage low enough not to kill.
How could they ban it?
What really intrigued the elder was the origin of that power.
Tianming had a sword spirit root, had he awakened a new spirit root like Feiyan?
No, that was impossible, two miracles couldn’t happen like that in such a short period of time.
’He must have consumed some kind of poisonous essence...’ Elder Tian concluded as he shook his head.
Tianming noticed the elder’s stare, but just ignored it, his remaining eye focusing on Qingyi.
His gaze was cold and murderous.
He had seen Qingyi fight and knew well that if that was all his power, it wouldn’t take more than a single blow to eliminate him.
’I can’t wait to see that bitch’s face as that damned pretty face melts under my poison!’ He exclaimed mentally as he glanced at Feiyan, imagining her begging for him.
Qingyi remained cold as his eyes met those of Tianming.
He could already imagine what was going through the young man’s mind and couldn’t help but laugh internally.
’Poison, huh?
You picked one of the worst things you could use to fight me,’ Qingyi thought.

His body of the primordial dragon basically made him immune to any kind of toxic substance, and even if he was affected, it wouldn’t take long for the strands of draconic Qi in his Dantian to purify the problem.
But there was still one thing that worried him: Tianming’s cultivation.
He simply couldn’t sense it, it was as if Tianming’s cultivation was far superior to his own, to a level that Qingyi had difficulty even sensing his aura.
’That’s going to be dangerous...’
"He seems to have quite a lot of hatred for you." Bao Zhang asked, noticing Qingyi’s gaze.
"Yes, I stole Feiyan from him." Qingyi laughed lightly, feeling the bronzed beauty tremble in his arms as Bao Zhang’s eyes widened.
Long, awkward moments passed without a word being spoken.
"That’s not a joke, is it?" Bao Zhang asked, his eyes alternating between Feiyan and Qingyi without stopping.
Qingyi was a beautiful man.
In fact, if the sect had a ranking of the most attractive men, he would appear in first place; if he claimed to be second, no one would dare declare themselves first.
But even so, he was far from having the status of a young master of the Xu family.
The Xu family itself was a duke-level family of the Golden Sun Kingdom, an entity that was only a single step behind the Ascending Dragon Sect.
If their patriarch reached the Burning Blood Realm, he probably wouldn’t fall behind the three great sects of the outer region of the Blue Moon Continent.
How on earth could Feiyan choose someone like Qingyi over young master Xu?
Qingyi ignored Bao Zhang’s question and they just focused on the battles that followed, making the man sigh heavily and also mind his own business.
Lei Feng and Jun Hao, however, didn’t miss that conversation; their gazes towards Qingyi getting even brighter.
Their junior brother really was a great man!
They would never have imagined stealing the wife of a young man as rich and powerful as Xu Tianming!
"Are you worried?" Qingyi whispered in Feiyan’s ear.
The beauty hadn’t said a word since the moment she saw Tianming, her eyes filtering him with coldness.
Feiyan listened to Qingyi’s words, her eyes remaining distant for a moment until she plucked up the courage to speak.
"I want you to surrender to him before the battle begins..." She finally spoke, turning her face towards Qingyi’s.

The only time he had seen her like this was when he took her as his wife.
Since then, she had always remained the smiling, seductive Feiyan who wasn’t shaken by anything.
"His cultivation... is already at the fourth stage, and has a powerful base.
Even I can barely sense it... please... you don’t have to fight it," she finally said, her eyes watering.
Qingyi paused for a moment, closed his eyes, felt his heart burn, but didn’t lower his head.
"You have too little confidence in me, dear...
He would have to be at least at the seventh stage of the Foundation Realm to frighten me." Qingyi spoke, hugging her comfortingly.
Her face sank into his chest, staining his white robes as he lovingly stroked her hair.
Despite his confidence, Qingyi’s eyes were cold.
Fourth stage Foundation Realm... how the hell had that bastard advanced so far in such a short space of time?

’System, can that be a threat to me?’ he asked.

chapters.title: Chapter 43 - The inner disciples selection (05)
paragraphs: "Begin!" Elder Tian’s voice echoed through the arena.
"Please instruct me well, Senior Brother Xiaohu." Qingyi clenched his fists, his body filled with a cloud of electric sparks before he advanced.
Xiaohu responded with a smile, his body surrounded by a sea of burning flames.
’He also has a movement technique?’ Qingyi blinked in surprise.
That kind of technique was rare, usually only inner disciples possessed it. He hadn’t expected to see someone with an ability similar to his own.
Unfortunately, he didn’t have much time to think about it.
Xiaohu’s body disappeared in an explosion of embers as he ran around Qingyi, his speed no slower than the lightning steps.
The next moment, a fireball appeared in his hand, tearing through the air towards Qingyi.
Qingyi stopped his steps momentarily, feeling a wave of heat hit his face before brandishing his sword.

The Thunderclouds Sword’s blade cut through the fireball, causing the flaming Qi to spread out in sparks that narrowly missed his body, falling a few meters behind and raising a thick curtain of smoke.
Taking advantage of the smoke cover, Qingyi activated his draconic eyes and could clearly see Xiaohu launching a relentless sequence of attacks at him.
"That bastard’s Qi is infinite?" Qingyi grunted, halting his steps and activating the lightning steps.
He launched himself towards Xiaohu while turning his body and swinging the thundercloud sword.
"You’re fast!" Xiaohu laughed, lowering his body.
Qingyi’s sword passed inches from his back, tearing only a piece of fabric.
"You too," Qingyi’s eyes cooled. "But it’s time to get serious."
Without waiting for an answer, Qingyi activated the lightning steps, channeling all his Qi into his legs.
His body turned into a blur, the Qi of the thundering sword dancing around him as he easily overcame Xiaohu’s movement technique.
"Shit!" Xiaohu tried to dodge, but it was too late.
Qingyi’s sword hit his shoulder and he was thrown violently to the ground.
Qingyi did nothing more, just stepped on Xiaohu’s chest and directed his gaze at Elder Tian.
The disciples reacted with astonished murmurs as they watched the scene.
Xiaohu, the most powerful fire cultivator among the sect’s outer disciples, had been defeated by Qingyi, who was two cultivation levels below and supposedly had far inferior talent.
How could that even be possible?
"Xiaohu loses, Qingyi advances," declared Elder Tian with an approving smile.
Qingyi then returned to Feiyan’s side.
After their second battle, things flowed smoothly.
In his third fight, Qingyi faced a beautiful ice cultivator, but he wasn’t fooled by her delicate appearance.
With a precise and powerful kick, he threw her out of the arena without hesitation.
In the fourth battle, he fought against a cultivator wielding a heavy, large axe.
Qingyi dueled with him for long minutes until he managed to drive his sword into his opponent’s belly, ending the fight.
By the time he had reached the fifth battle, he had gained total respect among the sect’s outer disciples.
A young man with no background who had received the golden token, conquered an incomparable beauty and was now successively defeating opponents with a higher cultivation than his.
"I surrender!" The young swordsman in front of Qingyi declared, bowing his head before leaping out of the arena.
He had only gotten this far by luck, facing weak opponents.
It was better not to fight Qingyi now and simply focus on the battle for the last remaining spots after the semi-finals.
Qingyi ignored the young man and just waited for the semi-finals. His eyes briefly met those of Tianming, who had just finished his own battle.
It wasn’t long before it was Qingyi’s turn to fight again in his sixth battle.
Her opponent was an ordinary-looking girl of delicate stature, carrying an ornate golden fan.
’An enchantment arts cultivator...’ Qingyi smiled slightly.
He had seen this girl fight before, using a strange pinkish Qi to deceive her male opponents’ senses and sneak up on them.
"Senior Brother Qingyi, please have mercy," she smiled seductively, revealing her cleavage as she assumed a seemingly fragile position.
’Good tactic... but that won’t work on me.’ Qingyi laughed, and the girl’s face distorted in astonishment as he advanced rapidly towards her.
He didn’t even draw his sword; the scabbard would suffice.
A crash echoed as he thrust towards her face, hitting one of her cheeks and sending her flying with a few teeth missing from her mouth.
Many male disciples cast angry glances in Qingyi’s direction as they watched the delicate girl being taken to the sect’s medical pavilion.
Didn’t that man respect beautiful women?
Returning to the stands, Qingyi exchanged glances with Bao Zhang.
"Then I’m the cruel one," Bao Zhang shook his head. "At least I had a good reason."
Qingyi laughed at those words. He had indeed been cruel; he could have aimed for the belly or the chest.
Going straight for the face had certainly been merciless.
But he didn’t think about it for long, his gaze taking on a cold expression.
"Be careful of Tianming. He’s promised to kill me, and the mere fact that you’re by my side could make him take aim at you too. Surrendering isn’t a bad idea," Qingyi warned Bao Zhang.
"Worry more about yourself, junior brother. I can handle myself," Bao Zhang replied, sprinting towards the arena.
He had seen Tianming fight and, although he wasn’t sure of victory, he trusted that he would at least be able to protect his own life against a one-eyed man.
"Are you a friend of Long Qingyi’s?" Tianming asked, his voice calm and composed.
A faint smile took over his cold face, his black robes fluttering as his remaining eye twinkled softly as he stared at Bao Zhang.
"We’re acquaintances," Bao Zhang replied, taking up a battle stance.
"Good!" Tianming’s smile intensified, his voice almost animated before changing completely, taking on an icy tone charged with murderous intent. "It’ll be quick, don’t worry."
The moment Tianming’s voice fell silent, Bao Zhang’s eyes went wide.
He seemed to be floating...
Why could he see his own body?

chapters.title: Chapter 44 - It’ll be quick
paragraphs: Bao Zhang’s head fell onto the cold marble floor, his eyes becoming opaque, a pool of blood forming beneath him as his powerful body collapsed to its knees.
Shock ran through the audience of disciples and even the elders and instructors.
Deaths happened in the arena frequently, as long as they didn’t occur after an elder had ordered the fighting to stop, killing was entirely allowed.
In the cruel world of cultivation, it was part of everyday life.
But that didn’t diminish the shock of the outer disciples.
Tianming didn’t even try to hide his murderous intent or pretend it was an accident.
He attacked to kill, his blade cutting with such speed that most of the disciples couldn’t even see it.
Only the elders and disciples at the highest stages of the foundation realm were able to perceive Tianming’s attack.
It was terrifying.
"NO!" Jun Hao roared, his eyes filling with tears as he threw himself into the arena, Lei Feng following soon after.
It was against the rules and they would possibly be severely punished for invading the arena without permission, but they didn’t care.
Kneeling over Bao Zhang’s body, Jun Hao tried to move him and grabbed it’s head.
In desperation, he tried to push healing pills into it’s mouth, joining the decapitated head to the body.
It was obvious that this wouldn’t work. Bao Zhang had been beheaded.
Perhaps if a divine doctor was nearby, it would be possible to revive him if the head was reattached to the body in time.
But that was out of the question.
The sect had only one divine doctor, and he wouldn’t bother with the treatment of just any outer disciple.
"Husband..." Qingyi felt Feiyan’s delicate hands grab his, they were warm and slightly trembling, squeezing tightly.
But he ignored her.
He had never felt any anger or animosity towards the young master of the Xu family. He just thought he was pathetic.
But that changed when he saw Bao Zhang’s decapitated body.
Suddenly, he felt his heart tremble, a hatred he had never experienced before taking hold of him.
Since arriving in this world, he had never killed any human being, nor did he even have any plans to kill unless it was necessary.
But he decided. Xu Tianming would die that day.
Ignoring Feiyan’s requests, he jumped into the arena.
Bao Zhang’s body had already been removed and all that remained was for him and Tianming to decide who would be the winner.
Qingyi sighed heavily as he circulated his Qi, feeling every muscle in his body tense up.
He had never been forced to really sweat and give it his all.
He never got to the point of straining his muscles until they almost ruptured, or of making his dantian tremble and his meridians burn.
But now he didn’t hold back.
The power of the corruption dragon god bloodline and the primordial dragon’s body. He put it all out.
The air around him shook, his aura extending beyond his body, electric lightning bolts charged by the lightning sword’s Qi tearing through the marble floor.
His face no longer bore the gentle, friendly and calm smile of a pure and humble Taoist.
Now it was arrogant, cold and filled with murderous intent, his black eyes glowing with a purple so pure and deep that it seemed capable of lighting up a night sky.
"What? Angry because I killed your little boyfriend?" Tianming teased, drawing his own sword.
A poisonous aura surrounded the young master’s body, the sword’s Qi dancing tenuously through this aura, the ground beneath his feet melting slightly.
"Begin!" Elder Tião’s voice echoed through the arena.
The next moment, Qingyi raised his the thunderclouds sword.
A metallic clang echoed, followed by an explosion of sparks as two slashes split, passing through Qingyi and tearing up the ground behind him for dozens of meters, leaving a deep gash in the marble.
Qingyi was forced to take two steps back, smoke billowing from where the attack had landed.
Raising his gaze, he saw Tianming with his sword drawn, his single eye showing surprise.
"Oh... I didn’t expect you to defend that." The young master smiled. It was the same blow he had used to kill Bao Zhang.
He really hadn’t expected Qingyi to be able to react in time, but that didn’t change anything.
Qingyi didn’t reply, just watching Tianming for long seconds before finally opening his mouth.
"It’ll be quick. Don’t worry."
The moment Qingyi’s voice fell, he activated the lightning steps and his body disappeared.
"Where?" Tianming’s remaining eye went wide, losing sight of his opponent.
Qingyi attacked from the right, the thundercloud sword tearing through the air with a sharp hiss.

Tianming raised his own sword on instinct, feeling his bones crack and his muscles scream as he tried to parry the blow, being forced to take more than ten steps backwards before finally standing his ground.
"Good!" Tianming roared. "I didn’t expect it to be that strong, I’ll enjoy killing you even more!"
Qingyi just ignored those words, but didn’t advance immediately, feeling the air around Tianming turn violent, his already powerful aura exploding even more.
He seemed to be finally giving it his all too.
Their swords met with a loud clang, the ground cracking beneath their feet, the marble floor sinking with the pressure of their cultivations.
For a brief moment, they found themselves at an impasse.
Qingyi felt his body burn and his meridians scream at the endless stream of energy flowing through them.
But he continued to push, his eyes focused on Tianming as he pushed more lightning Qi towards his sword, the rays flowing towards his opponent.
"Fuck!" Tianming grunted at the pain in his hands, but didn’t back down.
Moving his feet, he kicked towards Qingyi, his sword separating briefly from the handsome young man’s before he threw it again.
Qingyi turned his body, narrowly dodging a lethal blow, but was still unable to stop Tianming’s sword from tearing through his shoulder.
An explosion of blood stained his clothes.
It wasn’t lethal, but it was all Tianming believed he needed, his poisonous Qi flowing through the sword into Qingyi’s wound.

chapters.title: Chapter 45 - An incomparable technique
paragraphs: The outer disciples’ arena was filled with murmurs as everyone watched the final duel of the inner disciples’ selection.
Tianming was incredible.
Although his cultivation was only at the fourth stage of the Foundation Realm, his real power rivaled that of a seventh stage cultivator.
But it wasn’t him who caused these murmurs.
It was Qingyi. With his cultivation of the first stage of the Foundation Realm, he didn’t just fight Tianming head-to-head, he forced him to retreat.
Hua Feiyan felt her heart tremble every time their swords met.
Qingyi was winning, but she couldn’t help but feel a tightness in her chest.
Why did Qingyi have to fight like this? Why not just surrender? He was already guaranteed a place as an inner disciple!
After the arena, if Tianming tried anything, she could simply protect him.
As a core disciple, she had been given techniques and artifacts that would allow her to crush that bastard easily.
She bit her lips as she stretched out her hands, an aura of earth Qi rising in her palm.
What if she attacked Tianming right there? She didn’t need to kill him, just open a gap for Qingyi to finish the job.
She would be punished for intervening, but nothing that would lead to her death.
She hesitated, not for fear of punishment, but for how Qingyi would react. Would he be angry at her for intervening in his revenge? Would he blame her?
Then she felt a gentle, wrinkled hand fall on hers, and the Qi seemed to be suddenly swept away.
"I approve of your husband," Madame Xue’s calm, gentle voice penetrated her ears.
"He’s one of the most talented young men I’ve ever seen, and if he gets the spirit root enhancement pill, he’ll probably be someone who will make the outer region of the Blue Moon Continent tremble."
Feiyan didn’t get excited. "B-but what if he dies?" Her voice sounded shaky and depressed.
"Do you think you intervening will make anything better? The sect won’t do anything to you, I’ll protect you, but your husband has no protection at all.
If you intervene, it will be he who will suffer the punishment, and the sect’s punishment for this crime is death." Madame Xue closed her eyes.
"There’s nothing you can do but pray."
Feiyan shuddered, but finally just hugged her master.
The battle was approaching its climax.
Tianming and Qingyi’s bodies were covered in bruises and deep cuts as they fought, their clothes reduced to tattered rags that barely covered their sweaty, bloody skins.
"Die, you bastard!" Tianming snarled, launching an endless flurry of blows towards Qingyi, but nothing was enough.
No matter how much force he put into his sword, how much poisonous Qi he pushed towards the wounds that were accumulating on his opponent’s body, Qingyi simply wouldn’t budge.
It was as if his poison had no effect on him.
How could that be possible?
Qingyi wasn’t in a good position either.
He had already been pushing his body to the limit for long minutes, his vision beginning to darken as his draconic eyes glowed non-stop and his Dantian was rapidly drained of all Qi.
He needed to end this battle, and fast.
Gritting his teeth, he stomped hard on the ground, activating the Lightning Steps, sending so much Qi into his legs that they went numb.
He threw himself towards Tianming, raising his sword.
A metallic clang echoed and Tianming’s body went flying.
He felt the bones in his left arm break, along with some of his ribs, flying more than a hundred paces until he fell.
With difficulty, he knelt down, his eye twitching as he raised his face to look at Qingyi.
’Impossible...’ he thought.
How could he lose like that? He had tried so hard, sacrificed so much!
Why couldn’t he manage a single victory against Qingyi?
Was he really destined to be an eternal loser?
He turned his face, watching Feiyan from a distance.
She had watery eyes, but her smile was bright, as if she had just been freed from the greatest weight she had ever borne in her entire life.
"No..." Tianming murmured, his eye meeting Qingyi’s gaze, which was no longer brimming with hatred.
Now cold and calm, he studied Tianming as if he were nothing more than a worm about to be crushed.
’I can’t lose like this!’ he roared internally, turning his face towards the audience and the obscure figure watching him with a disappointed look.
A memory popped into his mind.
He was in a dark forest, inside the trunk of a colossal tree.
"What exactly are you?" Xu Tianming looked up, feeling that strange Qi in his body.
It was poisonous Qi, a type he had never expected to have in his entire life.
"Hm... now that we’re connected, I don’t think it’ll be a problem to tell you." The dark figure smiled.
"I’m a traitor. My family is one of the most powerful in the Nine Peaks Basin."
His words were casual, but Tianming shuddered.
A cultivator from the Nine Peaks Basin? what would he be doing in such a remote place?
"But... what could you possibly want from someone like me?" Tianming asked.
He had received power from the man, but he still didn’t know the price he would have to pay.
"I want to steal your sect’s spiritual vein and I want you to kill its leader," the shadowy figure declared.
"I could do that myself, of course. Swatting your leader would be like swatting a fly, but my family will find me out the moment I use my power."
Kill the sect leader and steal the spiritual root? Tianming shuddered.
That was absurd. He was only in the Foundation Realm; killing the sect leader was obviously impossible.
Fortunately, the shadowy figure seemed to understand his concerns.
"Don’t worry, I’ll teach you an incomparable technique and help you with elixirs to quickly reach the Iron Body Realm.
With this technique, you only need to use it against him. Even if he’s one cultivation realm above you, you’ll still defeat him easily."
The dark figure stood up. "After I steal the spiritual vein, I’ll take you as my disciple to the Nine Peaks Basin, don’t worry."
Hearing those words, Tianming’s eyes lit up.
A technique capable of easily killing a cultivator at the peak of the Burning Blood Realm while the user was only at the Iron Body Realm?
Was that really possible?
